title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea — Adulis and the kingdom of Zoskales (§4-§6)
language_note: Original Greek, same work as arabia-01 and southasia-02 (different section) — the Periplus is the connective tissue source spanning three of the seven seed regions.
original_text_excerpt:
4. Μετὰ δὲ τὴν Πτολεμαΐδα τὴν τῶν θηρῶν ἀπὸ σταδίων ὡς τρισχιλίων ἐμπόριόν ἐστι νόμιμον ἡ Ἀδουλὶ, κείμενον ἐν κόλπῳ βαθεῖ κατ᾽ αὐτὸν τὸν νότον, οὗ πρόκειται νῆσος Ὀρεινὴ λεγομένη, τοῦ μὲν ἐσωτάτου κόλπου σταδίους ὡς εἰς πέλαγος ἀπέχουσα διακοσίους, ἐξ ἀμφοτέρων δὲ τῶν μερῶν παρακειμένην ἔχουσα τὴν ἤπειρον, ἐν ᾗ νῦν ὁρμεῖ τὰ καταγόμενα πλοῖα διὰ τὰς ἐκ τῆς γῆς καταδρομάς. Πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ ὥρμει κατ᾽ αὐτὸν τὸν ἐσώτατον κόλπον ἐν τῇ Διοδώρου λεγομένῃ νήσῳ παρ᾽ αὐτὴν τὴν ἤπειρον, ἐχούσῃ πεζῇ τὴν διάβασιν, δι᾽ ἧς οἱ κατοικοῦντες βάρβαροι κατέτρεχον τὴν νῆσον. Καὶ κατ᾽ αὐτὴν τὴν ἐν τῇ Ὀρεινῇ ἤπειρον ἀπὸ σταδίων εἴκοσι τῆς θαλάσσης ἐστὶν ἡ Ἀδουλὶ, κώμη σύμμετρος, ἀφ᾽ ἧς εἰς μὲν Κολόην μεσόγειον πόλιν καὶ πρῶτον ἐμπόριον τοῦ ἐλέφαντος, ὁδός ἐστιν ἡμερῶν τριῶν. Ἀπὸ δὲ ταύτης εἰς αὐτὴν τὴν μετρόπολιν τῶν Αὐξωμιτῶν λεγομένων ἄλλων ἡμερῶν πέντε, εἰς ἣν ὁ πᾶς ἐλέφας ἀπὸ τοῦ πέραν τοῦ Νείλου φέρεται διὰ τοῦ λεγομένου Κυηνείου, ἐκεῖθεν δὲ εἰς Ἀδουλί. Τὸ μὲν οὖν ὅλον πλῆθος τῶν φονευομένων ἐλεφάντων ἢ ῥινοκερώτων περὶ τοὺς ἄνω νέμεται τόπους, σπανίως δέ ποτε καὶ ἐν τῷ παρὰ θάλασσαν περὶ αὐτὴν τὴν Ἀδουλὶ θεωροῦνται. Πρόκεινται δὲ τοῦ ἐμπορίου καὶ κατὰ πέλαγος ἄλλαι νῆσοι μικραὶ ἐκ δεξιῶν ἀμμιναὶ πλείονες, Ἀλαλαίου λεγόμεναι, χελώνην ἔχουσαι τὴν εἰς τὸ ἐμπόριον φερομένην ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰχθυοφάγων.

5. Καὶ ἀπὸ σταδίων ὡσεὶ ὀκτακοσίων κόλπος ἕτερος βαθύτατος, οὗ κατὰ τὴν εἰσβολὴν ἐν δεξιοῖς ἄμμος ἐστὶ πολλὴ κεχυμένη, καθ᾽ ἧς ἐν βάθει κεχωσμένος εὑρίσκεται ὁ ὀψιανὸς λίθος, ἐν ἐκείνῃ μόνῃ τοπικῶς γεννώμενος. Βασιλεύει δὲ τῶν τόπων τούτων ἀπὸ τῶν Μοσχοφάγων μέχρι τῆς ἄλλης Βαρβαρίας Ζωσκάλης, ἀκριβὴς μὲν τοῦ βίου καὶ τοῦ πλείονος ἐξεχόμενος, γενναῖος δὲ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ καὶ γραμμάτων Ἑλληνικῶν ἔμπειρος.

6. Προχωρεῖ δὲ εἰς τοὺς τόπους τούτους ἱμάτια βαρβαρικὰ ἄγναφα τὰ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ γινόμενα, Ἀρσινοητικαὶ στολαὶ καὶ ἀβόλλαι νόθοι χρωμάτιναι καὶ λέντια καὶ δικρόσσια καὶ λιθίας ὑαλῆς πλείονα γένη καὶ ἄλλης μορρίνης, τῆς γινομένης ἐν Διοσπόλει, καὶ ὀρείχαλκος, ᾧ χρῶνται πρὸς κόσμον καὶ εἰς συγκοπὴν ἀντὶ νομίσματος, καὶ μελίεφθα χαλκᾶ εἴς τε ἕψησιν καὶ εἰς συγκοπὴν ψελίων καὶ περισκελίδων τισὶ τῶν γυναικῶν, καὶ σίδηρος ὁ δαπανώμενος εἴς τε λόγχας πρὸς τοὺς ἐλέφαντας καὶ τὰ ἄλλα θηρία καὶ τοὺς πολέμους. Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ πελύκια προχωρεῖ καὶ σκέπαρνα καὶ μάχαιραι καὶ ποτήρια χαλκᾶ στρογγύλα μεγάλα καὶ δηνάριον ὀλίγον πρὸς τοὺς ἐπιδημοῦντας καὶ οἶνος Λαδικηνὸς καὶ Ἰταλικὸς οὐ πολὺς καὶ ἔλαιον οὐ πολύ· τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ ἀργυρώματα καὶ χρυσώματα τοπικῷ ῥυθμῷ κατεσκευασμένα καὶ ἱματίων ἀβόλλαι καὶ καυνάκαι ἁπλοῖ, οὐ πολλοῦ δὲ ταῦτα. Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔσω τόπων τῆς Ἀραβικῆς σίδηρος Ἰνδικὸς καὶ στόμωμα καὶ ὀθόνιον Ἰνδικὸν τὸ πλατύτερον, ἡ λεγομένη μοναχὴ, καὶ σαγματογῆναι καὶ περιζώματα καὶ καυνάκαι καὶ μολόχινα καὶ σινδόνες ὀλίγαι καὶ λάκκος χρωμάτινος. Φέρεται δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν τόπων ἐλέφας καὶ χελώνη καὶ ῥινόκερως. Τὰ δὲ πλεῖστα ἐκ τῆς Αἰγύπτου φέρεται εἰς τὸ ἐμπόριον τοῦτο ἀπὸ μηνὸς Ἰανουαρίου μέχρι τοῦ Σεπτεμβρίου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀπὸ Τυβὶ ἕως Θώθ· εὐκαίρως δὲ ἀπὸ Αἰγύπτου ἀνάγονται περὶ τὸν Σεπτέμβριον μῆνα.

reference_translation:
§4 Below Ptolemais of the Hunts, at a distance of about three thousand stadia, there is Adulis, a port established by law, lying at the inner end of a bay that runs in toward the south. Before the harbor lies the so-called Mountain Island, about two hundred stadia sea-ward from the very head of the bay, with the shores of the mainland close to it on both sides. Ships bound for this port now anchor here because of attacks from the land. They used formerly to anchor at the very head of the bay, by an island called Diodorus, close to the shore, which could be reached on foot from the land; by which means the barbarous natives attacked the island. Opposite Mountain Island, on the mainland twenty stadia from shore, lies Adulis, a fair-sized village, from which there is a three-days' journey to Coloe, an inland town and the first market for ivory. From that place to the city of the people called Auxumites there is a five days' journey more; to that place all the ivory is brought from the country beyond the Nile through the district called Cyeneum, and thence to Adulis. Practically the whole number of elephants and rhinoceros that are killed live in the places inland, although at rare intervals they are hunted on the seacoast even near Adulis. Before the harbor of that market-town, out at sea on the right hand, there lie a great many little sandy islands called Alalaei, yielding tortoise-shell, which is brought to market there by the Fish-Eaters.

§5 And about eight hundred stadia beyond there is another very deep bay, with a great mound of sand piled up at the right of the entrance; at the bottom of which the opsidian stone is found, and this is the only place where it is produced. These places, from the Calf-Eaters to the other Berber country, are governed by Zoskales, who is miserly in his ways and always striving for more, but otherwise upright, and acquainted with Greek literature.

§6 There are imported into these places, undressed cloth made in Egypt for the Berbers; robes from Arsinoe; cloaks of poor quality dyed in colors; double-fringed linen mantles; many articles of flint glass, and others of murrhine, made in Diospolis; and brass, which is used for ornament and in cut pieces instead of coin; sheets of soft copper, used for cooking-utensils and cut up for bracelets and anklets for the women; iron, which is made into spears used against the elephants and other wild beasts, and in their wars. Besides these, small axes are imported, and adzes and swords; copper drinking-cups, round and large; a little coin for those coming to the market; wine of Laodicea and Italy, not much; olive oil, not much; for the king, gold and silver plate made after the fashion of the country, and for clothing, military cloaks, and thin coats of skin, of no great value. Likewise from the district of Ariaca across this sea, there are imported Indian iron, and steel, and Indian cotton cloth; the broad cloth called monache and that called sagmatogene, and girdles, and coats of skin and mallow-colored cloth, and a few muslins, and colored lac. There are exported from these places ivory, and tortoise-shell and rhinoceros-horn. The most from Egypt is brought to this market from the month of January, to September, that is, from Tybi to Thoth; but seasonably they put to sea about the month of September.
translation_source: Wilfred H. Schoff translation (1912), with emendations from Lionel Casson's 1989 Princeton edition, hosted by ToposText.
citation_original: https://el.wikisource.org/wiki/Περίπλους_της_Ερυθράς_Θαλάσσης (ed. C. Müller, Geographi Graeci Minores I, Paris 1855; public domain)
notes: This is the first surviving external (Greco-Roman) written reference to Aksum by name ('Auxumites') and its king (Zoskales, usually identified as an early Aksumite ruler) — a direct textual complement to the Ezana Stone and the Aksumite coinage records (africa-01, africa-02). Strong triangulation set: a Roman merchant's travel account, a royal Aksumite inscription, and Aksumite numismatic evidence, all converging on the same Red Sea polity.
reference_translation_note: Replaced 2026-08-10. The previous text was an abridgement: it elided most of each section with '...', carried an editorial gloss ('[Aksumites]'), and gave the sections in the order §4, §6, §5 — so §6, the passage that lists what was imported into and exported from Adulis, had no aligned English and resolved as ENGLISH: NONE AVAILABLE in Part 7. Now Wilfred H. Schoff's 1912 translation of §4, §5 and §6 in full and in order, taken from the ToposText digitisation (topostext.org/work/491) already named in translation_source; Schoff's translation is public domain. Two mechanical changes: ToposText's hyperlinks are reduced to their link text (e.g. 'Ptolemies', 'Zoskales'), and runs of whitespace are collapsed. Schoff's own spellings and section numbering are left as they stand. This closes the same defect Part 6 closed for south_asia/periplus-muziris.json.

subject_places.name: Adulis
subject_places.note: Confirmed against the Pleiades snapshot of 2026-08-10 on 2026-08-13: 39271, title 'Adouli', 15.262/39.659, 'settlement, port', -30..300 — the Eritrean Red Sea coast near Zula. Title search on the corpus's own spelling misses it; found under the Greek form.

subject_places.name: Ptolemais of the Hunts
subject_places.note: 39409 Ptolemais Theron 18.583/37.885, 'settlement, port, anchorage', -30..2099. §4 places it 3,000 stadia (~530 km) north of Adulis; the coordinate is ~370 km NNW, the right order and the right direction.

subject_places.name: Oreine
subject_places.note: 39404 'Oreine (island)' 15.464/39.751, island, -30..2100 — ~25 km NNE of Adulis, inside the gulf, matching §4's 200 stadia seaward. Two decoys refused on coordinate: 736994 'Patsonteos (Oreine)', a canal in Egypt at 29.750/31.250, and 741584, unlocated.

subject_places.name: the island called Diodorus
subject_places.note: Named in §4 as the older anchorage, in text recovered 2026-08-13. Pleiades 759556 'Diodorou' exists and is UNLOCATED, so it carries no coordinate and cannot be cached. Note also that the Periplus names a DIFFERENT Diodorus island at §25, in the Bab el-Mandeb strait; that one is not this one and must not be substituted.

subject_places.name: Coloe
subject_places.note: 39363 Koloe 14.709/39.553, settlement, -330..300 — inland, ~62 km SSW of Adulis and ~110 km NE of Aksum, which fits §4's three days inland and five more to Aksum. Refused on coordinate: 550659 Koloe and 550556 Gygaia/Koloe, both in Lydia; 554259 and 614708, both unlocated. Pleiades also attaches the name 'Koloe' to 403627899 Matara and holds 698596572 Qohaito, the two modern candidates for the site; 39363 is used because it is the entry Pleiades titles Koloe and dates to the Periplus.

subject_places.name: the Auxumites
subject_places.note: 39303 'A(u)xoume' 14.134/38.721, 'cultural-landscape, settlement', -30..2100. The same id `africa-01-ezana-stone` carries as its findspot and `africa-02-aksumite-coin` as its origin — the third use, and the reason those are separate blocks. §4: all the ivory is brought there and thence to Adulis.

subject_places.name: Cyeneum
subject_places.note: §4's district the ivory is carried through. Pleiades 40186 Kyeneion resolves and is UNLOCATED — the gazetteer holds the place and records no coordinate for it. The id was carried in this note rather than in the record until A6 added `unlocated`, because `gazetteer --check` refused an entry with no geometry and citing the id would have failed the build. It is now cited: the entry has a title, a date range and provenance, and only its location is missing.

subject_places.name: the Nile
subject_places.note: 727172 'Nilus (river)' 9.904/30.657, river, -6000..2100. §4 has the ivory coming from beyond it.

subject_places.name: the Alalaei islands
subject_places.note: 39281 'Alalaiou (islands)' 15.729/40.003, 'archipelago, island', -30..2100 — the Dahlak archipelago, NE of Adulis. Named in §4 as the source of the tortoise-shell brought to market by the Fish-Eaters, in text recovered 2026-08-13; before that this place was in Schoff's English and not in the Greek.

subject_places.name: Egypt
subject_places.note: 766 'Aegyptus (Roman imperial province)', locationPrecision 'related', attested -30..2100 — contemporary with the Periplus, which is why it is used where Pleiades 837 'Asia Minor' was refused for persia-02 (that one is attested 1700..1799, a modern cartographic label). Its representative point 31.201/29.910 is Alexandria's own coordinate, so this placement must render as an extent and never as a pin; see `has_area` in gazetteer.py.

subject_places.name: the Arsinoite nome
subject_places.note: §6's Ἀρσινοητικαὶ στολαί. 736893 'Arsinoites/Krokodeilopolites Nomos' 29.286/30.735, 'nome-gr, label', -330..640 — the Fayyum. Ἀρσινοητικαί is the NOME adjective, which is what chooses this over 39295 Arsinoe, a Red Sea station at 12.712/43.251 that is in the right region and is not the place the cloth is made.

subject_places.name: Diospolis
subject_places.note: §6's murrine, τῆς γινομένης ἐν Διοσπόλει. 786017 'Diospolis Magna/Thebai' 25.665/32.632, settlement — Upper Egyptian Thebes. Refused: 727111 'Diospolis Kato' and 730107 'Diospolis', both 31.260/31.573 in the Delta, and 216859, which a name search returns and which is Kabyle, in Bulgaria.

subject_places.name: Laodicea
subject_places.note: §6's οἶνος Λαδικηνός. 668290 Laodicea 35.519/35.777, 'settlement, port, settlement-modern', -550..2100 — Laodicea ad Mare, modern Latakia, whose wine is the export. The feature type 'port' is what confirms it. Refused: 668291 'Laodicea ad Libanum' 34.557/36.519, inland, and the several Anatolian Laodiceas a title search returns first.

subject_places.name: Italy
subject_places.note: §6's οἶνος Ἰταλικός. 1052 Italia 43.694/11.095, region, locationPrecision 'related', attested **-30..300** — contemporary. Refused: 452346 'Italia (region)' 38.393/16.198, which is 'precise' and therefore the more tempting of the two, but is dated -750..-330 — the archaic Italia of the southern toe, four centuries too early; and 992073 'Italia (Diocese)', unlocated. A precise coordinate for the wrong century is still the wrong place.

subject_places.name: the Calf-Eaters
subject_places.note: §5's Μοσχοφάγοι, from whose territory Zoskales' kingdom runs. A people, not a settlement; nothing resolves in either gazetteer under any form searched.

subject_places.name: Barbaria
subject_places.note: §5's ἡ ἄλλη Βαρβαρία, the far limit of Zoskales' rule — the Somali coast. **Pleiades 471890 'Barbaria' was examined and refused**: it sits at 40.020/9.084, which is Barbagia in Sardinia. A name match would have taken it and drawn a Roman-African trade network through the Mediterranean.
